newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military's sex scandal spreads to Air Force.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military's sex scandal spreads to Air Force.

text.p: A U.S. Air Force general said Thursday eight male instructors had been disciplined for sexual harassment since 1994 at Lackland Air Force Base, the Air Force's centre for basic training.
The disclosure was the first to implicate the Air Force in a growing scandal over sexual harassment at military installations.

Brig. Gen. Robert Courter, commander of the 37th Training Wing at Lackland, told reporters all the instructors had been removed from teaching posts and one had been jailed in 1994 for a year for adultery and making sexual advances toward female trainees.
The most recent incident occurred earlier this year, when an instructor who is now out of the Air Force was reduced in rank for having consensual sex with a trainee, he said.

"There are going to be incidents, but where we have those cases, we take action. I feel certain the American people can be confident that their sons and daughters are going to be safe in the Air Force," he said.

Lackland public affairs officer Maj. Carla Sylvester said all Air Force recruits received their basic training at the San Antonio base, which was also a centre for technical training. She said about 75,000 Air Force members were trained there annually.

The issue of sexual harassment in the military came to light last week when the Army said a captain and two others who trained recruits had been charged with offences that included the rape of female trainees at the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland.
On Wednesday an Army drill sergeant at Fort Leonard Wood Army Base in Missouri was ordered confined for five months after he admitted having sex with three female recruits.

In response to the incidents, Defence Secretary William Perry said Wednesday he had ordered all branches of the military to reinforce a policy of "zero tolerance" for the harassment of women in uniform.
Sylvester said Air Force policy forbade any sexual relationships between instructors and trainees.

Meanwhile, the San Antonio Express-News reported that five drill sergeants at Fort Sam Houston had been disciplined for kissing, licking and dancing with female recruits during a February bus trip to Mexico.
Three of the sergeants were kicked out of the Army and two others reprimanded and removed from the drill sergeant programme, Fort Sam Houston spokesman Phil Reidinger told Reuters.

They supposedly engaged in "body shots" with the recruits, an activity in which salt, lime juice and tequila are sprinkled on one person's neck and chest and licked off by another, the newspaper said.

Reidinger said the bus trip was part of a regular programme in which recruits were recruits were taken to Nuevo Laredo, Mexico, 150 miles southwest of San Antonio, for recreation but the trips had been cancelled after the February incident.
Fort Sam Houston is the Army's largest medical training facility, with 38,000 students taking classes each year, Reidinger said.
